decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts sit inside the firm's core wafer-level packaging competence and fit its multifunctional packaging direction, so they meet aspirations at low incremental cost.
Carrier wafers for smaller diameters extend the established carrier line and support the strategic push toward reusable carriers, so there is no performance shortfall prompting search.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship launched at SEMICON and aligned with the advanced-packaging trend, so management will protect it while its results mature, as long as slack allows.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand is a flagship channel close to the core that uses existing standard substrates, so carrying it costs little and it broadens market reach.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and their results are uncertain, which makes them the likeliest candidate for problemistic reallocation, but they share glass-processing know-how and there is no clear evidence of failure, so the firm likely keeps them for now.
